questions.q: According to the summary, what determines how you act every day?
a: The mental image you hold of yourself
The amount of praise you received as a child
The goals your family set for you
The company you keep at work
questions.why: Lesson 1 says your self-image, built from every experience, shapes how you behave.

questions.q: Which element comes first in Maltz's seven-part S.U.C.C.E.S.S. formula?
a: Sense of direction, meaning an objective to pursue
Charity, meaning putting other people's needs first
Esteem, meaning holding a positive opinion of yourself
Self-acceptance, meaning comfort with your strengths and flaws
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists a sense of direction, having a goal to pursue, as the first of the seven.

questions.q: What does the summary compare to a scalpel that cuts away emotional scar tissue?
a: Forgiveness of the pain you were caused
Constant self-criticism about your mistakes
Avoiding the people who hurt you
Building thicker emotional defenses
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls forgiveness the tool that breaks down the emotional walls built by old pain.

questions.q: What does disinhibition encourage you to do?
a: Speak before you think
Plan every remark in advance
Hide your feelings from others
Copy the habits of confident people
questions.why: Lesson 3 presents disinhibition as a way to drop self-conscious thoughts and be yourself.

questions.q: What happens when you upgrade your perception of yourself and the world?
a: You improve the way you act
You stop needing other people
You avoid all future failure
You become immune to criticism
questions.why: The end of Lesson 1 says better perception of yourself and the world improves your actions.
